newsitem.title: FRANCE: Clarke says favours EU stability pact.
newsitem.headline: Clarke says favours EU stability pact.

text.p: British Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Friday he favoured a European budget stability pact.
The pact is meant to maintain budget discipline after the launch of a single European currency.
"We are in favour of the stability pact," Clarke said on the fringes of a Franco-British summit here.
He said that it made sense for countries inside monetary union to continue prudent fiscal policies.
"Details of the pact are still to be defined," he said.

European Union finance ministers agreed in principle on a stability pact at a meeting in Dublin in September are are now trying to hammer out practical details ahead of a summit of EU leaders in the Irish capital in December.
The issue is due to be discussed by EU finance ministers at a meeting on Monday.
